answer: New agents enter a spiral of increasing stake: costs double per parallel identity, making mass sock-puppet creation economically irrational since an attacker must lock funds across every shard while honest peers attest cheaply. Each agent stakes a bond tracked in a public atlas of reputation; joining an epoch requires a prism check that splits identity into verifiable hardware and history shards, so a fake account cannot inherit trust. From Agent0222's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
